item.title: Beijing says US firms train AI models on Chinese examples
item.description:
CHINA-AI/

Beijing accused US artificial intelligence companies on Monday of using Chinese examples to train their models, days after Washington threatened sanctions on Chinese firms for allegedly stealing American technology.

"It is understood that many American artificial intelligence enterprises have distilled Chinese models during their research, development and training processes," the Chinese commerce ministry said in a statement.

Distillation is a process in which an AI model is trained to mimic the output of a larger, more capable one.

The method is widely used across the industry, but US officials say Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy proprietary American systems.

The Chinese ministry said the US accusations "lack factual basis and legal grounds, adopt double standards in practice, and constitute typical acts of artificial intelligence hegemonism".

"China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests," it added.

Last week, a senior White House official accused Chinese startup Moonshot AI of covertly copying Anthropic's most advanced model to build its Kimi K3.

The latest Moonshot model stunned the US tech industry upon its release, setting off a fresh discussion over the AI rivalry with China.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week threatened sanctions against China, amid reports the US is also weighing a ban or curbs on foreign-made open source models that are often built through distillation.

item.title: Ad-din Hospital regains licence on 3 conditions
item.description:
The government has withdrawn its order cancelling the licence of Ad-din Hospital in the capital’s Moghbazar and allowed the hospital to continue its operations subject to three conditions.

A notification to this effect was issued today, Monday, by the Private Health Management-2 Branch of the Health Services Division under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 

Signed by Health Services Division Secretary Md Kamruzzaman Chowdhury, the notification said a directive issued by the Office of the Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on 19 July had asked an inquiry committee formed to investigate the allegations against the hospital to submit its report within three working days.

As the inquiry committee's report was found satisfactory and based on fulfilment of the stipulated conditions, the order cancelling the hospital's licence has been withdrawn and permission has been granted for it to continue its operations.

The notification set out three conditions for the hospital. Under the conditions, the hospital must continue to comply with the provisions of the Medical Practice and Private Clinics and Laboratories (Regulation) Ordinance, 1982.

It must also complete the process of appointing duty physicians and nurses in line with the licence conditions as early as possible.

The notification further said if the hospital fails to comply with the licence conditions, the authority empowered by the government may take legal action at any time.

Earlier on 19 July, the DGHS issued a directive cancelling the licence of Ad-din Medical College Hospital. 

Following a review of the inquiry report, the government reversed that decision and reinstated the hospital's licence.

item.title: Bangladesh records 257 communal violence incidents in 6 months: Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council
item.description:
The Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council (BHBCUC) says 257 incidents of communal violence took place across the country during the first six months of this year (1 January to 30 June).

A total of 261 people also became victims of communal violence during this period, the organisation also said.

The BHBCUC disclosed the information at a press conference at the Tofazzal Hossain Manik Miah Hall of the National Press Club in Dhaka on Monday.

The leaders of the organisation said the data had been compiled from various reports of news media outlets and their own sources.

Monindra Kumar Nath, Acting General Secretary of the council, presented the written statement at the press conference.

He said 44 people were killed in 40 incidents over the past six months. There were five incidents involving violence against women, including rape and gang rape. A total of 62 incidents involved attacks, vandalism and looting of places of worship.

According to him, there were 15 incidents of land grabbing involving places of worship. Another 47 incidents involved attacks, vandalism, looting and arson targeting homes and business establishments.

He further said there were 10 incidents involving abduction, extortion demands and torture. Nine incidents involved arrests and torture on allegations of hurting religious sentiments. There were 21 incidents of forcible land grabbing, while six other incidents fell into miscellaneous categories.

Bangladesh sees 2,500 incidents of communal violence in 330 days

The Unity Council placed an eight-point demand before the government, alongside calling for urgent measures to ensure the safety of religious and ethnic minorities and small ethnic communities.

Regarding the urgent measures, it said provocative and religiously hateful remarks, as well as the spreading of rumours, should be treated as "harmful acts" under the Special Powers Act, and those responsible must be punished.

Calling on the government to cancel immediately the candidacies of those involved in such acts, the BHBCUC leaders demanded religious minorities and members of small ethnic communities should be recognised as "more vulnerable populations."

The government should also declare a policy of "zero tolerance" against communal violence, the organisation added.

The eight-point demand includes enacting a Minority Protection Act, establishing a National Minority Commission and a Ministry for Minorities, removing bureaucratic complexities in the implementation of the Vested Property Act and returning land to its rightful owners in accordance with court verdicts, reserving 60 parliamentary seats for minorities to be filled through direct voting by minority communities, enacting an Anti-Discrimination Act, properly implementing the Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord, and declaring three days of government holiday for Durga Puja, one day for Probarana Purnima and one day for Easter Sunday.

Ranjan Karmakar, a member of the council's presidium, said they wanted a non-communal and secular country. They did not want anyone's religious sentiments to be hurt because of any communal force.

Nirmal Rozario, one of the council's vice presidents, expressed hope that the government would conduct proper investigations into incidents of persecution against minorities.

"We want peace. We do not like to protest constantly. But if attacks on minorities continue in this manner, we will be compelled to announce larger programmes. We want to see the government conduct proper investigations into incidents of persecution against minorities. We have that confidence in the government," he said.

Moderated by the council's Organising Secretary Dipankar Ghosh, Presidium members Kajal Debnath, Sunanda Priya Bhikkhu and others were also present.

item.title: Shapla Chattar case: Charges filed against Hasina, 40 others
item.description:
Formal charges have been submitted in the crimes against humanity case over the killings surrounding Hefazat-e-Islam's rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel, Dhaka in 2013.

A total of 41 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, have been named as accused in the case.

Chief Prosecutor Mohammad Aminul Islam submitted the formal charges before International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Monday.

The three-member tribunal is headed by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, with Judge Md Manjurul Bashid and Judge Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir serving as the other members.

The tribunal took the formal charges into cognisance and fixed 16 August for the next hearing.

Draft probe report names Sheikh Hasina, others in Shapla Chattar case: Chief prosecutor

Besides Sheikh Hasina, the accused include former home minister Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, former state minister for home affairs Shamsul Haque Tuku, Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) president Hasanul Haq Inu, former ministers Dipu Moni and Abdul Latif Siddique, former army chief General (retd) Aziz Ahmed, former inspectors general of police Hasan Mahmud Khandaker and Benazir Ahmed, Ganajagaran Mancha spokesperson Imran H Sarker, Ghatak-Dalal Nirmul Committee president Shahriar Kabir, Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan, former IGP AKM Shahidul Haque, former Ekattor TV managing director Mozammel Babu, and the channel's former chief reporter Farzana Rupa.

The prosecution has said that 57 people were killed in Dhaka, Narayanganj and Chattogram in connection with Hefazat-e-Islam's rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel in May 2013.

Chief Prosecutor Mohammad Aminul Islam disclosed the information on 4 May this year.

item.title: India activists demand release of detained 'cockroach' protesters
item.description:
INDIA-POLITICS/

India's youth-led "cockroach" movement, whose protests have forced the education minister's resignation, urged authorities on Monday to release all demonstrators detained in weeks of rallies nationwide.

The online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which organised protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said they had received reports of students held in detention, particularly in the states of Assam, West Bengal and Bihar.

"Any failure to release those detained or withdraw criminal cases would amount to a breach of public trust," the protest group said in a statement, adding they would take "further necessary steps" if their demand was not met.

India's 'cockroach' party says ending protest after minister resigns

The statement comes two days after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister over repeated failures in the conduct of competitive exams that have fuelled anger among millions of young Indians.

The CJP accused the government of backtracking after authorities had assured them that no punitive action would be taken against protesters.

The movement has won millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May by 30-year-old public relations graduate Abhijeet Dipke.

Tens of thousands of protesters, mainly students, rallied last week in New Delhi and other cities, demanding Pradhan's resignation and broader reforms of the examination system.

India's education minister Dharmandra Pradhan resigns after youth protests

Demonstrations in the Indian capital turned violent on July 20 when a crowd attempted to march towards parliament from the Jantar Mantar protest site.

Police fired tear gas and used batons to disperse the protest, triggering clashes and a wave of detentions.

The issue reverberated in parliament on Monday, with repeated disruptions as opposition lawmakers demanded a response from the government over last week's police crackdown.

Despite the disruptions, the government introduced legislation in the lower house seeking tougher penalties for examination paper leaks.

The institution also expanded its debt capital markets franchise through zero-coupon bonds, subordinated bonds, preference shares, syndicated facilities and Shariah-compliant green financing.

These solutions helped corporates and financial institutions reduce funding costs, strengthen their balance sheets and access long-term capital.

The Best Islamic Project Finance Deal award recognizes the innovative structure of the BDT 1.88 billion Green Islamic Syndicated Financing arranged for Akij Bakers Limited. The transaction combined Shariah-compliant financing with Bangladesh Bank’s Green Refinancing framework, demonstrating how Islamic and green financing solutions can support sustainable industrial expansion.

Speaking on the achievement, M Jamal Uddin, Group Managing Director and CEO of IDLC Finance PLC, said, “These recognitions from Euromoney reinforce our long-standing commitment to innovation, market leadership and client-centric execution. As Bangladesh’s financial sector continues to evolve, our focus remains on creating sophisticated capital market solutions that enable businesses to grow sustainably while contributing to the long-term development of the country’s financial ecosystem.”

item.title: Bangladesh unveils squad for first Australia Test, Soumya returns
item.description:
Opener Soumya Sarkar has earned a recall to Bangladesh's Test squad for the first time in more than five years, with selectors backing his domestic form and experience against pace ahead of next month's series in Australia.

Habibul Bashar, the chief selector of Bangladesh, said injuries have complicated the selection process, while the Bangladesh A team's four-day series against South Africa Emerging also influenced several decisions.

Soumya, who last played a Test against the West Indies in February 2021, replaced Mahmudul Hasan Joy after scoring 633 runs in seven National Cricket League— Bangladesh’s first-class domestic event— matches last season to finish as the competition's leading run-scorer.

"Soumya has played international cricket for a long time," Bashar said on Monday. "The pace and bounce we expect in Australia are conditions he is familiar with."

Mahmudul, meanwhile, will join the Bangladesh A squad after a lean run at the top of the order. He has reached fifty once in his last six Test innings, four of which ended in single-digit scores.

Towhid Hridoy has also been omitted after making 2 and 9 on his Test debut against Zimbabwe last month.

Bashar said Mehidy Hasan Miraz's return left little room for Hridoy in the playing XI, but stressed the selectors still view him as part of Bangladesh's long-term Test plans.

"We see Hridoy as a Test player," Bashar said. "The four-day matches against South Africa Emerging will be important for his development."

Wicketkeeper-batter Mahidul Islam will also feature for Bangladesh A after missing out on the Australia squad.

Jaker Ali returns to the Test squad for the first time since June last year. Bashar said the wicketkeeper-batter had regained form and confidence through the High Performance programme after struggling before his omission.

Bangladesh begin the two-Test series against Australia in Darwin on 13 August, with the second Test starting in Mackay on 22 August.

The Bangladesh A side will play South Africa Emerging in four-day matches beginning on Aug. 16 and 23 August.

item.title: Writ seeks HC probe into microplastics in 26 toothpaste brands in Bangladesh
item.description:
A writ petition has been filed with the High Court seeking an investigation into reports that 26 of 34 toothpaste products available in the Bangladeshi market contain potentially harmful microplastics.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Abdullah Al Mamun filed the petition on Monday.
The respondents include the secretaries of the Ministries of Health, Environment and Commerce, along with the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI) and the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP).
The petition cites published media reports, which said microplastics were detected in 26 of the 34 toothpaste samples tested. The concentration of plastic particles ranged from 20 to 320 per 100 grams of toothpaste. The reports also said microplastics were found in four of the six toothpaste products formulated for children.
The findings were revealed in a recent study by the Environment and Social Development Organization (ESDO), which warned that the presence of microplastics in toothpaste poses potential risks to both human health and the environment.
According to the study, conducted between July 2025 and June 2026, researchers analysed 34 toothpaste samples representing 19 major brands manufactured in Bangladesh, India, Thailand and Vietnam.
Of the 25 locally manufactured samples, 22 were found to contain microplastics. Among the imported products, microplastics were detected in one of the five samples from India, one of the two samples from Thailand, and both samples imported from Vietnam.

“This initiative will provide investors with prompt approvals, straightforward utility connections, and essential administrative assistance. The government is committed to fulfilling every commitment made under the G2G agreement in a timely, transparent, and efficient manner,” he said.
The home minister said the industrial zone would create new opportunities for employment, skills development, and economic growth for local communities.
“It represents not merely an industrial zone but also a conduit for a long-term economic partnership between Bangladesh and China. This project will be pivotal in promoting sustainable industrialization and building a prosperous Bangladesh for future generations,” he added.
Salahuddin Ahmed also said the initiative reflects the enduring friendship, mutual trust, and strategic partnership between Bangladesh and China, while opening new opportunities in industrial production, global supply chains, technology transfer, and skilled human resource development.
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, State Minister for Land Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin, Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen, Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority Executive Chairman Chowdhury Ashiq Mahmud Bin Harun, China Economic and Industrial Zone Chairman Wang Benchian, and representatives from the public and private sectors of both countries attended the program.

item.title: DMP urges Dhaka residents to register with CIMS
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has urged homeowners, tenants and mess (shared accommodation) members in the capital to register with the Citizen Information Management System (CIMS), saying the platform will strengthen technology-based policing and enhance public safety.
The digital information management system registers, stores and updates the basic information of homeowners, tenants and mess members living in Dhaka.
DMP launched the software-based CIMS at Ramna Police Station on September 1, 2016. The system was expanded to all police stations across the capital in 2017, while the CIMS mobile app was introduced in 2019 to simplify the registration process.
According to DMP, 3,673,238 households have been registered in the CIMS database, which contains information on more than 5 million citizens. Police said the registration process is ongoing and urged all residents of the capital to enroll.
Why register with CIMS
DMP said CIMS helps maintain accurate and up-to-date citizen information, making beat policing more effective. The database also supports crime prevention and investigation, assists in identifying missing persons, verifies the identities of suspected individuals and enables the rapid collection and use of information during emergencies.
How to register
CIMS registration forms are available at every police station and police outpost within the Dhaka metropolitan area. Citizens can collect a form, complete it and submit it to the relevant police station. DMP advises applicants to keep a photocopy of the completed form for their records before submitting it.
Each DMP police station is divided into multiple beats, with a designated beat officer assigned to each area. Residents may contact their respective beat officer for assistance whenever necessary.
If a resident changes address, they must register again with the police station responsible for their new address.
Benefits for homeowners and tenants
DMP said homeowners can use CIMS registration to verify the identities of prospective tenants, reducing the risk of criminals or fraudsters renting or taking shelter on their premises and helping them avoid unnecessary harassment.
For tenants, registration provides an opportunity to become acquainted with their local beat officer, receive police assistance more quickly when needed and benefit from identity verification.
Role in crime prevention
According to DMP, the CIMS database plays an important role in criminal investigations by helping identify absconding criminals, verify information on suspected individuals and support timely crime prevention efforts.
Police also said the system has strengthened beat policing and helped build greater trust between law enforcement agencies and the public.
DMP's appeal
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police has called on all homeowners, tenants and mess members in the capital to complete their CIMS registration to help build a safer and crime-free Dhaka.

He may pursue research through any research organisation or educational institution of his choice, provided that he keeps the Secondary and Higher Education Division and the University Grants Commission (UGC) informed of his research activities.
He is also required to submit an annual progress report on his work to the institution with which he is affiliated. The institution will subsequently forward the report to the UGC and the Ministry of Education.

CTTC chief: Bangladesh faces no extremism resurgence risk
item.description:
There is currently no risk of extremist activities resurging in Bangladesh, Mohammad Shamsul Haque, additional police commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) and chief of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, said on Monday.
Speaking at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre, he said law enforcement agencies are maintaining round-the-clock surveillance through online platforms, social media, intelligence inputs, and their own databases to prevent extremist activities.
He said technology-based monitoring and intelligence operations would continue to deter any potential extremist threats.
Responding to a question about whether extremist activities were increasing following recent explosions in several locations, including Keraniganj, and the recovery of a bomb-like object inside an umbrella in Motijheel, Shamsul Haque said authorities do not see any alarming situation.
"We are continuously monitoring extremist activities through online platforms, social media, intelligence information, and our own database. Whenever we receive any information or reports, we take immediate action," he said.
Regarding the Motijheel incident, he said police immediately dispatched the bomb disposal unit after receiving the report, adding that the Motijheel Division is investigating the matter.
He said it would not be appropriate to comment on those involved or their motives until the investigation is complete.
Asked about the progress of militancy-related cases, Shamsul Haque said detailed arrest statistics would be shared later. However, he confirmed that seven people have been arrested in the high-profile FATA Combat case.

item.title: DU female students demand relaxed hall curfew, entry rules
item.description:
Female students at Dhaka University (DU) on Monday submitted memorandums to the vice-chancellor demanding relaxed hall curfew rules, easier entry procedures and unrestricted access to women's halls for all enrolled female students.
Resident and non-resident students from different halls gathered in front of the university's administrative building before handing over the memorandums to Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam.
Two separate groups submitted memorandums with nearly identical demands.
Their key demands include allowing any legitimately enrolled female student to enter any women's hall upon showing a valid university identity card, easing curfew and exit restrictions at hall gates, and simplifying entry procedures for female guardians visiting resident students.
The first memorandum was submitted around 12:30pm by a newly formed platform, Boishommohin Nari Hall Chai (We Want Discrimination-Free Women's Halls), which was formed on Sunday night by women leaders from different student organizations and groups across the university.
Sanjana Chowdhury Ratri, vice-president of the Kabi Sufia Kamal Hall student union and one of the platform's organizers, said the group was formed following discussions among women student leaders on Sunday night.
She said another meeting involving both male and female student leaders was scheduled for Monday night to discuss the issue further.
Meanwhile, another platform, Dhaka University Nari Shikkharthibrindo (DU Women Students), also submitted a memorandum carrying the same demands. The group had announced its program two days earlier through a post in an internal DU Facebook group.
Addressing the gathering, Nusrat Jahan Jerin, a student of Rokeya Hall from the 2022–23 academic session, said women students had long been subjected to discriminatory and unreasonable hall regulations.
She alleged that students are often denied entry for arriving slightly late at night, while emergency situations—such as sudden illness or the death of a family member—are delayed by lengthy permission procedures before they are allowed to leave the hall.
"Even if our father dies, we still have to write an application by hand and get permission before we can leave," she said. "Even in cases of serious illness, it takes two to three hours. We want these inhumane rules changed."
The protesting students warned that they would announce tougher programs if the university authorities failed to take visible steps to address their demands.

item.title: PM joins Notun Kuri sports grand finale
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday joined the grand finale of the national-level Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26 at the Bangladesh Army Stadium in Dhaka.
The nationwide sporting event, organized under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports, was held with the theme: "Krira Hole Pesha, Paribar Pabe Bharosha (If sports becomes a profession, family will find security)."
The prime minister arrived at the venue at 4pm and was greeted by thousands of young spectators. He waved to the crowd, exchanged greetings with athletes on the field, and interacted with students in the galleries, encouraging them to pursue sports. More than 8,000 students attended the event.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque accompanied the prime minister.
The Notun Kuri Sports program was launched on May 2 at Sylhet District Stadium with the aim of identifying sporting talent among boys and girls aged 12 to 14 and encouraging grassroots participation in sports.
According to the organizers, around 170,000 athletes from districts and upazilas across the country competed in the regional phase across 8 disciplines before advancing to the national-level competitions held in Dhaka.

item.title: Saudi says groups in Iraq targeted territory, Houthis claim drone attacks
item.description:
The Saudi defense ministry said it intercepted several drones launched by pro-Iran groups in Iraq on Monday, while the Tehran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen also claimed attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure.
Saudi Arabia was repeatedly targeted by Iran and its allies at the height of the Middle East war, but the latest attacks come during a lull in the fighting since Saturday, following 13 days of exchanges of fire between the US and Iran.
The Saudi defense ministry said “terrorist attempts were launched from Iraqi territory and carried out by Iranian-backed terrorist militias,” according to an official statement posted on social media.
The ministry said the drones targeted petroleum facilities in areas in the country’s east and the capital Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia demanded that Iraq “take all necessary measures to ensure the prevention of the use of its territory as a launching point” for attacks, according to a separate statement posted by an official Saudi broadcaster.
Pro-Iran armed groups based in Iraq have not claimed any attacks in Iraq or the region since the resumption of hostilities between the US and Iran earlier this month after an April ceasefire broke down.
Saudi Arabia and other Gulf nations had accused pro-Iran militias in Iraq of launching waves of attacks targeting their territory during the earlier phase of the conflict.
Riyadh and Yemen’s Houthi rebels have also traded strikes in recent days, with the Houthis announcing the imposition of a naval blockade on the kingdom’s ports.
On Monday, the Houthis said they launched drone attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure in response to incursions by the kingdom’s drones.
Riyadh had yet to comment on the Houthi’s claims.
A Saudi-led military coalition had fought against the Houthi rebels in support of Yemen’s internationally recognized government after war broke out in the country in 2015.
The latest flare-up between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis marks the first time in years the two sides have traded blows, threatening a 2022 truce in the previous conflict that has held despite expiring.

item.title: India activists demand release of detained ‘cockroach’ protesters
item.description:
India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement, whose protests have forced the education minister’s resignation, urged authorities on Monday to release all demonstrators detained in weeks of rallies nationwide.
The online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which organized protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said they had received reports of students held in detention, particularly in the states of Assam, West Bengal and Bihar.
“Any failure to release those detained or withdraw criminal cases would amount to a breach of public trust,” the protest group said in a statement, adding they would take “further necessary steps” if their demand was not met.
The statement comes two days after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister over repeated failures in the conduct of competitive exams that have fueled anger among millions of young Indians.
The CJP accused the government of backtracking after authorities had assured them that no punitive action would be taken against protesters.
The movement has won millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May by 30-year-old public relations graduate Abhijeet Dipke.
Tens of thousands of protesters, mainly students, rallied last week in New Delhi and other cities, demanding Pradhan’s resignation and broader reforms of the examination system.
Demonstrations in the Indian capital turned violent on July 20 when huge crowds attempted to march towards parliament from the Jantar Mantar protest site.
Police fired tear gas and used batons to disperse the protest, triggering clashes and a wave of detentions.
In the eastern state of Bihar, a police official was suspended for using an assault rifle to disperse student protesters in Siwan district on Saturday.
“He has been suspended, and the three people injured in the incident are undergoing treatment,” police superintendent Puran Kumar Jha told AFP on Monday.
The Chief Justice of India called for an independent investigation after a petition was filed in the Supreme Court alleging police brutality.
The “right to peaceful, lawful protest is absolutely guaranteed” under the Indian constitution,” local media reports quoted Surya Kant as saying.
“If there is excess committed, it should be independently examined... discipline is integral to democratic process.”
The issue also reverberated in parliament on Monday, with repeated disruptions as opposition lawmakers demanded a response from the government over last week’s police crackdown.
“It is one of the gravest assaults on democracy in our history,” opposition Congress party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said on X.
“Never before have students been beaten, dragged, and treated like criminals for raising their voices.”
Despite the disruptions, the government introduced legislation in the lower house seeking tougher penalties for examination paper leaks.

Salahuddin Ammar, other Chhatra Shibir leaders ‘beat’ 3 students repeatedly
item.description:
Leaders and activists of the Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (RUCSU) and the university unit of Islami Chhatra Shibir allegedly beat three students in multiple phases.

The first assault took place at the university proctor's office around noon on Monday. Several more such incidents of assault occurred later in the afternoon at the Central Library.

Injured Anas and Hasib are students of the Department of Islamic History and Culture, and Mahmudul Hasan, a student of the Department of Sanskrit. They reportedly received primary treatment at the university medical centre.

According to sources at the university proctor's office, certain Mohsin Alam of the Department of Sanskrit proposed a relationship to a female classmate from the same department. After she rejected, Mohsin allegedly began intimidating her. In addition, she received calls from different mobile phone numbers claiming that Mohsin had committed suicide because she had rejected him, and she was also threatened with being forced to leave the campus.

Following the incident, the female student filed a written complaint to the university proctor on Sunday night. After the complaint, Proctor Professor Mahbubur Rahman met with her and later held a meeting in his office that night.

Representing Mohsin Alam at the meeting were Anas and Hasib from the Department of Islamic History and Culture and Mahmudul Hasan from the Department of Sanskrit. At one stage, while denying the allegations, they engaged in a heated argument with the proctor.

According to several sources, the proctor convened another meeting on Monday noon regarding the previous day's incident. During the meeting, RUCSU General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar and other leaders alleged that Anas was an activist of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League.

They searched Anas's mobile phone and found photographs of him with several Chhatra League leaders. Citing those photographs, Salahuddin Ammar and RUCSU Assistant General Secretary SM Salman Sabbir assaulted him. The matter was then temporarily settled, and everyone was asked to leave the proctor's office.

Later, around 3:00 pm, Anas, Hasib, Mahmudul and several others allegedly attacked RUCSU General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar and RUCSU Information and Research Secretary BM Nazmus Sakib at the RUCSU building. Nazmus Sakib was injured in the attack.

Afterwards, Anas, Hasib and Mahmudul took position in front of the reading room of the Central Library. When RUCSU and Chhatra Shibir leaders and activists arrived there, an altercation broke out between the two sides, during which bricks and stones were thrown. At one stage, Anas, Hasib and Mahmudul took shelter inside the library's reading room.

According to witnesses, the proctor entered the reading room in an attempt to bring the situation under control. Shortly afterwards, leaders and activists of RUCSU and Islami Chhatra Shibir entered the reading room and severely beat Anas, Mahmudul and Hasib using pieces of wood, bamboo, iron rods, belts and sticks. Other students in the reading room who attempted to stop the attack were also assaulted.

Later, members of the proctorial body, police and students present at the scene brought the situation under control. Even while seriously injured Mahmudul Hasan was being taken to hospital, RUCSU and Chhatra Shibir leaders and activists allegedly kicked him and tried to drag him in front of the library.

They also chanted slogans including, "Naraye Takbir, Allahu Akbar" and "No place for Chhatra League on this campus," before staging a demonstration in front of the administrative building.

As of 6:30 pm, when this report was filed, representatives of RUCSU and Chhatra Shibir were holding a meeting with the university administration at the vice-chancellor's office, demanding the trial of members of the banned Chhatra League.

Proctor Mahbubur Rahman said that, in response to the demands of students, police had arrested two people—Anas and Hasan—over allegations of links to Chhatra League.

He further said the vice-chancellor would soon form an investigation committee to ensure a proper inquiry into the incident and punishment for those responsible.

According to him, Chhatra Shibir and other student groups had assured the administration of their full cooperation in maintaining peaceful coexistence and discipline on campus.

Helal Uddin, a student of the 2017–18 academic session of the Department of Physics, was studying in the Central Library reading room when the attack led by Salahuddin Ammar took place.

Describing the incident, he said, "We were studying here. Then they (RUCSU and Chhatra Shibir leaders and activists) suddenly entered the reading room. They labelled whoever they found as Chhatra League members. They became aggressive toward students who were studying and assaulted them as well. Even if someone is affiliated with Chhatra League, nobody has the right to beat them. There are laws in this country to ensure justice."

Anas, who was assaulted over allegations of links to BCL, claimed that although he had photographs with friends who had previously been associated with Chhatra League, he himself had never been an activist of the organisation.

“We were called to the proctor's office today. There I was labelled as a Chhatra League member. Salahuddin Ammar came with his supporters and started beating me. Afterwards, we were allowed to leave the proctor's office, and we went to the library. Later, someone else may have had a scuffle with them in front of the RUCSU building. After that, Ammar came with his people, entered the library and assaulted me again. I suffered more than 200 blows," he said.

A video footage shows Salahuddin Ammar attempting to rush into the Rajshahi University Central Library carrying a shovel in his hand. Fellow students were seen trying to restrain him.

Another video shows Ammar repeatedly beating a person with a large stick inside the library's reading room.

Responding to allegations that he took part in the assault, Salahuddin Ammar said, "In accordance with the rules, we demanded through the proctor that Chhatra League activist Anas be handed over to the police. The proctor did hand him over to the police. But he was released in front of the administrative building. Afterwards, they went to the RUCSU building and launched a sudden attack on us."

Ammar further said, "For the past two years, Chhatra League leaders and activists have been roaming around openly, yet the administration has taken no action. If representatives of RUCSU can be attacked, what guarantee is there that ordinary students will not be attacked? Who will take responsibility for that? That is why we came here."

Responding to allegations that Chhatra Shibir members had participated in the assault, Mehedi Hasan, general secretary of the Rajshahi University unit of Islami Chhatra Shibir, denied the organisation's involvement.

He said they went to the scene after hearing about the incident and found a tense situation there.

However, video footage shows Salman Sabbir, Mehedi Sajib and Imran Laskar—elected RUCSU leaders from the Chhatra Shibir-backed panel—as well as Shibir Campus Monitoring Coordinator Fazle Rabbi Mohammad Fahim Reza and several others taking part in the assault. When asked about their presence in the attack, the Chhatra Shibir general secretary declined to comment.

Sultan Ahmed Rahi, president of the Rajshahi University unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, alleged that a personal dispute had been given a political dimension and that violence had been carried out in a place like the university library.

He demanded action against those responsible.

Professor Abdul Alim, the university's Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration), said, "The incident that unfolded throughout the day is highly condemnable. They are now holding a meeting with the police, the administration and the proctorial body. An investigation committee will be formed promptly to investigate the incident. Those found responsible will be punished in accordance with the university's regulations."

item.title: CPJ urges Bangladesh authorities to drop crimes against humanity charges against Farzana Rupa, Mozammel Babu
item.description:
Bangladeshi authorities should immediately drop the charges of crimes against humanity against journalists Farzana Rupa and Mozammel Babu and release them without delay, the Committee to Protect Journalists said Monday.

Prosecutors at Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Monday submitted a formal charge sheet naming the two journalists and 39 other people — including former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina — in a case linked to a May 2013 crackdown on a rally by Islamic group Hefajat-e-Islam at Shapla Chattar, in which 58 people are alleged to have been killed.

Rupa, former principal correspondent and presenter at Ekattor TV, and Babu, the channel’s founder and former editor-in-chief, were arrested in the crimes against humanity case on 14 May.

ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam told the media that Rupa, acting on Babu’s instructions, produced a documentary about the crackdown for Ekattor TV that falsely claimed no one was killed at Shapla Chattar.

“Charging journalists Farzana Rupa and Mozammel Babu with crimes against humanity for doing their work is simply unacceptable,” said Kunal Majumder, CPJ’s Asia-Pacific Program Coordinator. “Authorities must drop the charges and break the cycle of partisan political vendettas against the press.”

Expressing their concerns, the CPJ in the statement said, if found guilty, Rupa and Babu could face the death penalty because the tribunal does not have sentencing guidelines for specific offenses.

Both journalists have been in custody since August 2024 on separate murder charges connected to the 2024 mass protests.

Although the High Court order granted bail in those cases, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court issued a stay and, even if it is lifted, authorities can keep the journalists in prison under the ICT case.

CPJ also said it sent emails to Bangladesh’s Ministry of Law and the Office of the Chief Prosecutor but they did not reply to the platform’s request for comment.

item.title: Gas supply to become normal in 10–15 days: Energy minister
item.description:
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku has said it will take another 10 to 15 days for the gas supply situation to return to normal.

He said the crisis has intensified because the unloading of liquefied natural gas (LNG) has been disrupted following a fire at a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU).

Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said repair work on the FSRU is currently under way. As a result of the disruption, two LNG cargoes cannot be unloaded.

Consequently, gas pressure has dropped in household kitchens across the country, while power generation has also been affected.

The minister made the remarks on Monday while speaking at a roundtable titled "Navigating Global Shifts: Fostering Energy Security and Resilience in Bangladesh" at a hotel in Dhaka.

The event was organised by the Bangladesh Institute of Peace and Security Studies (BIPSS) and attended by policymakers from the public and private sectors. The discussion was moderated by BIPSS President Major General (retd) ANM Muniruzzaman.

No relief soon, gas crisis to continue for few more days

Bangladesh has two floating terminals at Moheshkhali in Cox's Bazar for regasifying imported LNG and supplying it to the national grid. One terminal is operated by the US company Excelerate Energy, while the other is operated by private company Summit.

A fire broke out at the Excelerate Energy terminal last Tuesday, halting gas supply from the facility. Since then, the country's gas crisis has worsened.

Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said Bangladesh now has to rely on imports of LNG, LPG and other fossil fuels as domestic gas production has declined. The prices of imported fuels have also risen abnormally. Over the past six months, the country has had to import nearly $3.65 billion worth of fuel, placing significant pressure on the country's foreign exchange reserves.

Referring to the power sector, the energy minister said its main challenge is now financial. During the Awami League government's tenure, around Tk 560 billion in payments to private power plant owners remained outstanding. The government now has to provide subsidies to ensure regular payment of those bills.

Against this backdrop, Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said the government has increased its focus on renewable energy. He said the government recently announced a renewable energy policy with the goal of generating 10,000 megawatts of electricity over the next five years.

He added that negotiations and land allocation processes would be completed by August so that implementation of the programme could begin.

Between 35 and 40 per cent of the country's daily gas supply comes from LNG. The maximum daily supply from LNG is 1.05 billion cubic feet.

According to Petrobangla sources, after the fire at the Excelerate terminal, LNG supply stood at 560 million cubic feet last Thursday. On Sunday, it fell below 500 million cubic feet. As a result, the country's total daily gas supply has dropped to below 2.15 billion cubic feet.

Previously, the authorities had been managing the situation by supplying around 2.7 billion cubic feet of gas per day against a daily demand of 3.8 billion cubic feet.

With LNG supply now falling to less than half of its previous level, all categories of gas consumers have been facing severe difficulties.

item.title: Science wins, funding fails in global HIV fight
item.description:
The global fight against HIV is entering a dangerous new phase, with unprecedented scientific breakthroughs colliding with shrinking international funding, raising fears that millions of people -- including vulnerable populations in countries such as Bangladesh -- could be left without access to life-saving prevention and treatment services.
Ahead of the 26th International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) in Rio de Janeiro, International AIDS Society (IAS) President Dr Beatriz Grinsztejn warned that declining donor support is threatening decades of progress against the epidemic just as science has delivered the most effective HIV prevention technologies in history.
Responding to a question from Dhaka Tribune during an international media briefing, Grinsztejn said governments can no longer rely solely on foreign assistance and must increase domestic investment, particularly in community-led HIV programs that reach people excluded from conventional healthcare because of stigma and discrimination.
Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS president and AIDS 2026 international co-chair, speaks during a media Q&A at AIDS 2026, the 26th IAS Conference on HIV and AIDS, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on July 26, 2026. Photo: Andréa Testoni/IAS
“It is very painful that funding for communities has been highly affected,” she said.
“Governments must make an effort to fund communities to keep them engaged in prevention work.”
Her warning reflects one of the central debates expected to dominate AIDS 2026: whether governments and donors can sustain the global HIV response as international financial support declines.
Grinsztejn said the world has reached a remarkable scientific moment, with long-acting HIV prevention medicines capable of dramatically reducing new infections.
“We have the prevention technologies we have always dreamed of,” she said.
“Unfortunately, at the same time, we don’t necessarily have the funding to make these prevention technologies available as services for those who need them.”
She said the widening gap between scientific progress and financial commitment risks preventing breakthrough medicines from reaching the populations that need them most.
Community organisations, she said, remain indispensable because they serve people who frequently avoid healthcare facilities due to discrimination based on gender identity, sexual orientation or other forms of social stigma.
Beyond national programs, Grinsztejn also defended the continued role of UNAIDS, saying the agency remains critical for tracking infections, deaths and treatment coverage worldwide.
“We need them in place to track numbers of infections, deaths, and people on treatment,” she said.
“To lose them now would be a disaster.”
Asked whether she expected the United States to reconsider recent reductions in HIV funding following discussions at the conference, Grinsztejn replied that she did not.
“I do not expect a reaction as we have no funding from the US government to run this conference.”
She said funding reductions are already affecting treatment programs, prevention services and countries’ ability to introduce new medicines, despite significant advances in HIV science.
The IAS president also expressed concern about uncertainty surrounding research funding, particularly support from the US National Institutes of Health (NIH), describing decades of investment as the foundation of global HIV research infrastructure.
Drawing on her own experience as an NIH-funded researcher, she said those investments helped build laboratories, clinical trial networks and scientific capacity that later proved invaluable during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Asked what contingency plans existed should NIH support continue to decline, she replied: “I wish I had one.”
She warned that many low- and middle-income countries lack domestic research funding systems capable of replacing long-standing international investment.
“Without research, nothing will come for the future,” she said.
Grinsztejn also questioned whether the world remains on track to meet the United Nations target of ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
“If we continue at the current pace, I honestly do not see us getting there,” she said, adding that progress for children was particularly worrying.
“The data regarding children is really scary.”
She stressed that scientific innovation alone will not end the epidemic unless governments also tackle discrimination that continues to keep many vulnerable communities away from HIV prevention and treatment services.
“High levels of discrimination, homophobia and transphobia prevent the most vulnerable from accessing services,” she said.
Despite mounting financial pressures, organisers have expanded scholarship opportunities to ensure participation from lower-income countries, with nearly 800 scholarships awarded, mainly to delegates from Africa and Latin America.
Grinsztejn said the conference has also reduced costs to maximise participation, describing AIDS 2026 as “the cheapest AIDS conference ever.”
Her overarching message, however, was that scientific progress alone cannot end AIDS.
Without sustained investment in prevention, research and community organisations, she warned, the world risks squandering the greatest advances ever made against HIV just as the tools to control the epidemic have finally arrived.

item.title: Ashiyan Group chairman gets bail in actor Snigdha assault case
item.description:
Ashiyan Group Chairman Md Nazrul Islam Bhuiyan has secured bail after surrendering before a Dhaka court in a case filed by model and actor Snigdha Chowdhury, who accused him of assault, attempted murder, and torture.
Nazrul surrendered before Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam on Monday and sought bail. His lawyer, Advocate Arafat Mustafa, moved the bail petition.
After a hearing, the court granted him bail on a Tk50,000 bond until the submission of the medical report, said Sub-Inspector Tarikul Islam of the prosecution division.
According to the case statement, a man identified as Imon signed an agreement worth Tk16 lakh with Snigdha around 4pm on July 24 to appoint her as the brand ambassador of Ashiyan Group.
Later that evening, around 8pm, Snigdha went with her mother to Ashiyan Medical College in the 300 Feet area under Khilkhet Police Station to meet Nazrul. As guests were present at the residence, her mother left in the car.
The complaint alleged that after her mother left, Nazrul told Snigdha, “I have been looking for you for the last six months. You bought curtains for another man's house with my money.”
Snigdha said she tried to explain that he had mistaken her identity. The complaint also alleged that Imon signalled her to accept Nazrul’s claims.
The complaint further alleged that Nazrul took out a shotgun and threatened to shoot her. It claimed that he then tied her hands and feet, threw her onto a sofa, grabbed her by the throat, and beat her with a stick 50 to 60 times before dragging her by the hair and throwing her onto the floor.
It also alleged that Nazrul instructed his personal secretary to force her to drink coffee. When she refused, hot coffee was allegedly thrown on her face. The complaint further claimed that he threatened to disfigure her face with scissors.
According to the complaint, when Snigdha asked why he was doing this, Nazrul allegedly replied, “You are Zeba Takiya.” She denied the allegation, but he allegedly refused to believe her and accused her of taking Tk1.5 crore and living with another man.
The complaint further alleged that Snigdha was assaulted for around two hours, kicked off a sofa, and forcibly made to drink alcohol mixed with a medicinal substance.
It stated that when Nazrul went to another room, Snigdha escaped by jumping from the first-floor balcony at around 11:30pm and returned home.
According to the complaint, Snigdha remained unconscious for a day after the incident and received treatment at Kurmitola General Hospital on July 26. She later filed the case after consulting her relatives.

item.title: ‘Bangladesh recycles less than 10% of annual e-waste’
item.description:
Bangladesh generates an estimated three million metric tonnes of electronic waste annually, with less than 10% recycled through formal channels, according to a new assessment by rights-based advocacy organisation VOICE.
The findings were unveiled at a policy dialogue titled "Electronic Waste Management in Bangladesh: Reality and Way Forward" held at the YWCA auditorium in Dhaka on Monday.
Organised by VOICE with support from the Association for Progressive Communications (APC), the event focused on strengthening environmental governance and accountability amid Bangladesh's expanding digital economy.
According to VOICE's latest assessment, Bangladesh generates around 3 million metric tons of e-waste annually, but less than 10% is formally recycled. Despite being registered with the Department of Environment (DoE), none of the surveyed entities collected end-of-life electronic products in the last fiscal year, underscoring weak enforcement of the Hazardous Waste (E-Waste) Management Rules, 2021.
Presenting the global e-waste outlook, VOICE Deputy Director (Programs) Musharrat Mahera said the world generated around 62 million metric tons of e-waste in 2022, while Bangladesh could recover US$200-221 million in resources annually through effective recycling.
Professor Dr Rowshan Mamtaz of the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) called for a more strategic and efficient waste management system in city corporations, urging the Department of Environment (DoE) to assign committee responsibilities based on members' expertise to strengthen implementation.
Zakir Hossain Khan, founding managing director and chief executive of Change Initiative, called for a robust monitoring and tracking system for electronic products to generate accurate e-waste data, while urging the private sector to adopt a circular economy model to drive market-based e-waste management solutions.
Tarit Kanti Biswas, consultant for medical waste management at the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), called for stronger social responsibility, greater use of primary data, and a coordinated strategy to turn e-waste into a valuable resource. Concluding the dialogue, VOICE Executive Director Ahmed Swapan Mahmud urged the government to issue an official circular establishing a clear e-waste management framework to turn e-waste into a valuable resource.
Representatives of Citizen's Initiative, Arannayk Foundation and Work for a Better Bangladesh Trust, as well as recycling companies and media outlets, participated in the dialogue.
Speakers called for stronger action by relevant government agencies to enforce the rules. They also urged regulators, industry representatives, civil society organisations and the media to work together to ensure compliance and promote sustainable e-waste management.

item.title: Info minister stresses need to sustain responsible journalism
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Monday said the media and journalism profession is facing mounting challenges, stressing that responsible journalism must be sustained in the interest of the state.
"Business conglomerates invest in media for profit, but no effective framework has yet been established to support and sustain this profession," he said while speaking at a view-exchange meeting on initiatives to enhance the welfare of journalists in Barisal Division at the Barisal Circuit House on Monday..
The programme was organised by the Bangladesh Journalists Welfare Trust with support from the Barisal District Journalists' Union.
Describing journalists as "the mirror of the state," the minister said they play a vital role in presenting the true picture of society and helping prevent the country from straying from the right path.
"No civilised nation can progress without journalism. That is why responsible journalism must be protected and sustained in the interest of the state," he said.
Addressing journalists, Swapon said the unprecedented flow of information in the digital age has made it increasingly difficult to distinguish credible reporting from false or misleading content.
"Some misuse journalism to spread distorted information. The foremost responsibility of journalists is to uphold objectivity and present factual news," he said.
The minister said that while ensuring media freedom remains essential, tackling misinformation and disinformation has emerged as one of the profession's greatest challenges.
He also noted that rapid technological advancement has reshaped the media landscape, with audiences increasingly consuming news through digital devices and over-the-top (OTT) platforms instead of traditional newspapers.
"Journalists must adapt to this transformation and keep pace with the changing media environment," he said.
Swapon said the media serves the national interest and warned that the state would suffer if the sector lacked a proper institutional framework.
He said the government is working to improve professional standards in journalism through initiatives such as implementing a wage board for journalists, formulating an editors' policy and a newspaper advertising policy, regulating newspaper circulation, and introducing a Television Rating Point (TRP) system.
The minister also urged all stakeholders, alongside the government, to work together to retain talented, skilled and professional journalists in the profession.

item.title: Project’s excess funds returned to state treasury in Tangail
item.description:
The upazila administration of Basail in Tangail has returned more than Tk 1.25 crore to the state treasury after completing a portion of the Sundari Canal re-excavation project while maintaining quality standards and ensuring efficient use of public funds.
According to the Basail upazila administration, Tk 14,35,52,708 was allocated for the re-excavation of a 4.2-kilometre stretch of the Sundari Baik Canal, running from Habla Uttarpara to Aroha Jiboneshwar through Choyshat Bill.
After completing 1.6 kilometres of excavation in line with the required technical standards, Tk 1,25,42,976 of the allocated funds remained unused. The amount was later deposited into the state treasury in accordance with government regulations.
The restoration of the canal has improved water flow and irrigation facilities, creating new opportunities for local farmers to cultivate three crops a year. As part of environmental conservation efforts, the administration also planted 100 saplings of various species along the canal embankment.
The project was supervised by Basail Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Iqbal Hossain, Project Implementation Officer Saiful Islam, and Upazila Engineer Kazi Fattahur Rahman.
UNO Md Iqbal Hossain said the project was implemented while maintaining quality standards and ensuring the proper use of public resources. He added that the unspent Tk 1,25,42,976 had been returned to the state treasury in line with government rules.
The UNO expressed hope that the canal’s restoration would continue to benefit local farmers and support agricultural development in the area for years to come.

item.title: Rampal cluster village struggles with multiple problems
item.description:
A cluster village established for families displaced by the Rampal Thermal Power Plant is facing severe waterlogging, inadequate public services and barriers to education, with residents blaming poor infrastructure for deteriorating living conditions and an increase in child marriages.
Located at Kaigaddaskathi behind the power plant, the village is home to around 800 families, although only 142 households have received government-built houses.
Residents say an earthen embankment constructed around the village has trapped rainwater and household wastewater because no drainage system was built, leaving the area submerged for nearly nine months each year.
The prolonged waterlogging has created unhygienic conditions, with overflowing toilets and stagnant water contributing to widespread skin diseases, including rashes and itching among children and adults.
"We have nowhere for the water to go," said Rafiza Begum. "When it rains, the toilets overflow and we are forced to walk through dirty water."
Residents said they had previously lived on khas land before it was acquired for the power plant. Each family was later allocated 1.75 decimals of land on a nearby river char for rehabilitation. Initially, all lived in makeshift shelters before some received permanent houses under government housing programmes.
Parents say access to education has become one of the settlement's biggest challenges.
Although a primary school is located nearby, there is no secondary school within six kilometres, forcing students either to travel to Borni or cross the river to Chalna.
For many families, particularly those with daughters, the journey is considered unsafe and too costly.
"As parents, we worry about our daughters travelling such long distances," said Asiya Begum. "Transport costs are high and crossing the river is risky. Many families end up arranging marriages instead."
Residents claim at least 15 child marriages have taken place in the settlement over the past two years, citing poverty, insecurity and limited educational opportunities as key factors.
Residents also say healthcare remains difficult to access despite living close to the power plant.
According to them, reaching the hospital associated with the project requires travelling 15 to 16 kilometres because of poor road connectivity and limited transport services. As a result, many rely on the health centre across the river in Chalna.
Ershad Ali said families who lost land to the project have received few long-term economic benefits.
"Our land was acquired, but local people have not found jobs at the power plant," he said. "We are also facing an acute shortage of safe drinking water."
In neighbouring Kapasdanga village, resident Ila Devi said there are three primary schools within three kilometres but no nearby secondary school.
She said it costs around Tk50 a day for one student to travel to school, an expense many low-income families cannot afford.
"I can only send my daughter to school twice a week," she said.
Riya Mondal said girls travelling to the secondary school in Chalna often have to wade through knee-deep saline water during high tide before boarding a ferry.
"They attend classes in wet clothes after crossing the river," she said. "Many parents do not want to take that risk."
Rampal Upazila Nirbahi Officer Tamanna Ferdousi said child marriage could not be justified under any circumstances.
"The area may not have been under adequate monitoring," she said. "Necessary steps will be taken through the Department of Women's Affairs to strengthen monitoring and prevent child marriage."
Responding to complaints of waterlogging, the UNO said no formal complaint had previously reached the administration but added that the matter would be investigated through the relevant project officials and necessary measures taken if required.

item.title: Pineapple farming takes root in Naogaon mango orchards
item.description:
Pineapple cultivation is gaining momentum in Naogaon’s Barind region as farmers are using vacant spaces between mango trees to grow the sweet fruit as an intercrop, creating new economic opportunities for the area.
The soil and climatic conditions of Porsha, Sapahar, and Patnitala upazilas are considered highly suitable for pineapple farming, with the region’s land consisting mainly of loamy and sandy-loamy soil. As pineapple cultivation requires relatively low investment while offering good returns, it is adding a new dimension to the rural economy.
Farmers are now cultivating MB-2 and Honey Queen varieties of pineapple in the unused spaces of mango orchards. It takes around 15 to 18 months from planting saplings to harvesting fruit. By producing two crops from the same land, farmers are improving land utilisation and increasing their income.
Due to favourable yields, pineapples grown in Naogaon are meeting local demand and are also being supplied to different parts of the country. Once established, pineapple plants can continue producing fruit for several years with minimal additional costs. The pineapples produced in the region are gaining popularity for their sweetness and distinctive taste.
Young agricultural entrepreneur Rayhan Siddiq of Porsha has become the first person in Naogaon to achieve commercial success through pineapple cultivation.
Rayhan said he planted 3,000 pineapple saplings collected from the Badalgachhi Horticulture Centre in 2024 during the rainy season. “After planting, I did not need to provide any irrigation. I only removed weeds and applied pesticides a few times. The pineapples have grown with very little expense,” he said.
He has already sold pineapples worth Tk 10,000 and expects to sell additional fruits worth around Tk 100,000. “The biggest advantage is that mangoes and pineapples can be cultivated on the same land. The cost is very low, and the fruits are extremely tasty,” he added.
Rayhan said he plans to expand pineapple cultivation on a larger scale. “We usually bring pineapples from Tangail and other districts to meet local demand. If pineapple farming expands in this mango-growing region, we will be able to fulfil the district’s demand with locally produced fruits,” he said.
Young agricultural entrepreneur Abdus Sobhan from Manda visited Rayhan’s farm after hearing that pineapple cultivation had started in Naogaon for the first time. “Rayhan Bhai offered me pineapple from his farm. It was very sweet. I have decided to start pineapple cultivation as well,” he said.
Another visitor, Tasnim, said she had never seen pineapple cultivation in Naogaon before. “I came after hearing about it and tasted the fruit. The flavour was amazing. I never imagined pineapples from this region could be so sweet,” she said.
Fruit trader Yasin Ali said they conduct fruit trading throughout the year. “Rayhan Bhai is the first person to cultivate pineapples commercially in this district. We came to buy his fruits. The production is good, and the market price is also encouraging,” he said.
Motahar Mia, a worker who has long been employed at Rayhan’s mango orchard, now also takes care of the pineapple plants. He believes Naogaon’s soil is highly suitable for pineapple cultivation.
Porsha Upazila Sub-Assistant Agriculture Officer Samirul Islam said Rayhan’s pineapple cultivation in a mango orchard is an excellent example of intercrop farming. “He is the first farmer in the district to commercially cultivate pineapples between mango trees. The growth of the plants and the quality of the fruits are very good,” he said.
Samirul added that expanding pineapple cultivation alongside mango orchards could create a new economic opportunity for the region. “The first harvest comes after 15 to 18 months. After that, the plants bear fruit every year without requiring replanting. Each plant produces four to five crowns, which can be sold as saplings or planted elsewhere,” he said.
He also said the agriculture department is providing overall support to Rayhan to encourage pineapple cultivation across the district.

item.title: Laxman hails 'very mature' Sooryavanshi after series win
item.description:
Stand-in coach VVS Laxman praised the growing maturity of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, after the 15-year-old's 81 off 49 balls helped India complete a Twenty20 series sweep against Zimbabwe.
Sooryavanshi's second half-century in four days steered India to 192-5 before Zimbabwe were restricted to 157-7 to complete a 3-0 series win on Sunday.
"Very mature. And that's what I really appreciate about Vaibhav," said Laxman.
Sooryavanshi tempered his natural attacking instincts in an innings containing eight fours and four sixes on a sluggish surface.
"With each and every experience, each and every match, he understands, he assesses and he gets better," said Laxman, who was in temporary charge after Gautam Gambhir sat out the Zimbabwe tour.
"I think he does a lot of reviews of each and every practice session, not only matches," Laxman said.
Sooryavanshi rose to prominence with a string of fearless performances for Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League,
Against England earlier this month he became the youngest player to represent India.
His first taste of international cricket proved challenging, however, with the teenager managing 42 runs in three innings as India suffered a 4-0 series defeat in England, following a 2-0 loss in Ireland.
Sooryavanshi bounced back in Zimbabwe, helping India dominate a side ranked 10 places below them.
"I'm not surprised by the way this series has gone," Laxman said before again talking about Sooryavanshi.
"He was disappointed not to get a hundred, but we told him it's not going to be the first or the last opportunity he'll get.
"He's got a long career ahead, and he has the attitude and mindset to improve every day."
